messages:
amanda: follow-up proposal: lightweight edge resume for streaming clients. goal: distinguish transient client disconnects from backend faults without large state. core idea: ephemeral per-connection ring buffer + resume token that encodes seq + kv-checkpoint. default resume window 5s, buffer cap 32KB.

raj: curious about hedging interplay. if we start a hedge to fallback model, resumed client could see duplicated or out-of-order tokens. how guard?

sylvia: attach monotonically increasing chunk_seq inside resume token. hedged responses include their base seq. edge compares and fast-forwards or drop overlapping chunks. requires chunk-level idempotency at edge.

tom: large concern: memory at scale. millions of sockets x 32KB = bad. propose heuristic: enable resume only when client opts-in via header `x-rwd-resume: 1` and hints expected chunk rate. otherwise use stateless short-path (no resume).

amanda: opt-in makes sense. also add per-gateway soft memory cap and per-tenant quotas, evict LRU sessions when exceeding. record metrics: resume_enabled, resume_hit, resume_miss, resume_evicted.

raj: operational: how to measure false positives where edge resumes but backend has applied side-effects? we need a correctness check.

sylvia: backend should expose a tiny endpoint `/resume-check` that validates resume_nonce against backend kv-version. response: {resume_ok, backend_kv_version}. edge proceeds only when resume_ok true. if backend doesn't implement, edge falls back to checkpoint-restart path (409 + checkpoint id).

tom: alternative to avoid backend changes: edge can conservatively abort and re-issue request to backend to re-play from last safe checkpoint. costlier but backward-compatible.

amanda: agree. migrate to resume-check gradually; default to conservative fallback when missing. add a feature flag for resume-check enforcement.

raj: draft invariants for RFC follow-up: - ordering preserved for resumed sessions - at-most-once side-effect guarantee if backend resume_check confirms - otherwise at-least-once after checkpoint restart - memory bounded by gateway caps + per-tenant eviction.

sylvia: implementation notes: reuse session-affinity metadata store to hold small circular buffer pointers and resume_nonce. don't introduce new distributed storage. local buffers can be ephemeral in router process; if router restarts or moves, resume fails and client gets 409. document this as expected behavior.

amanda: edge cases: slow-chunking clients (eg long-poll) should default to non-resumable to avoid holding buffers. we'll provide guidance in docs. also consider adding `x-rwd-checkpoint` header for backends that already emit checkpoints.

deploy-bot: Feature flag created: feature/edge-resume-proto, rollout window 2026-04-02..2026-04-09. :rocket:

raj: action items: I'll write the RFC follow-up with invariants + state diagram. sylvia/tom: prototype buffer LRU + session-store extension. amanda: write header + resume-check API spec. sync Wed 9am PT.
